ideas.rawText: On the Microns med-spa system I decided nothing would send raw PHI to a third-party model. Text goes through a de-identification pass first that swaps identifiers for stable tokens like [PATIENT_123] and [PHONE_1]. The model reasons over tokens, and the response is re-identified on the way back so the patient still hears their own name. I wrote in the code that this is the identifier-stripping half of HIPAA Safe Harbor for the outbound prompt specifically — a strong technical control, not a substitute for a BAA and Zero Data Retention on the vendor account. Run all three. [SOURCE: microns-ai-system/backend/app/services/deidentify.py — VERIFY AND REWRITE IN YOUR OWN WORDS]

ideas.rawText: I did not trust my own scrubber. The LLM wrapper raises a PHILeakError if a prompt still carries identifiers at send time. The scrubber can be wrong; the hard check at the boundary catches it. I would rather the call fail loudly than leak quietly. ideas.rawText: A detail that cost me time on the de-identification work: pattern order matters. The first pattern to match a span owns it. Emails have to be matched before phone numbers, because an address can contain a run of digits. SSNs before phones, because both are digit groups with separators. Get the order wrong and the scrubber quietly mangles the wrong thing. [SOURCE: microns-ai-system/backend/app/services/deidentify.py — VERIFY AND REWRITE IN YOUR OWN WORDS]

ideas.rawText: The rule I keep coming back to: degrade instead of failing. With no API key, or when the model provider is down, the Microns system falls back to a deterministic rule engine. It still books appointments and still scores leads. It just stops paraphrasing. The business function survives the outage. [SOURCE: microns-ai-system/backend/app/services/llm.py — VERIFY AND REWRITE IN YOUR OWN WORDS]

ideas.rawText: Model choice by job, not by prestige. Latency-sensitive conversational turns get the small fast model. Review responses and ambiguous qualification answers get the bigger one. Most of the reliability came from the routing around the models, not from which model I picked. [SOURCE: microns-ai-system/backend/app/services/llm.py — VERIFY AND REWRITE IN YOUR OWN WORDS]

ideas.rawText: The lead qualification path is six questions, a 0-100 score, and a routing decision: hot, warm or cold. The scoring is boring on purpose. A number a human can argue with beats a model that says 'this lead seems promising'. [SOURCE: microns-ai-system/backend/app/services/lead_service.py — VERIFY AND REWRITE IN YOUR OWN WORDS]

ideas.rawText: When I specified my own LinkedIn content agent, I made it a hard rule that it can never write 'comment WORKFLOW and I'll send you the blueprint' or 'DM me'. Not because the copy is bad, but because the system has no comment automation and no messaging. A CTA the system cannot deliver on is a lie, so the quality gate blocks it before it can be published.
